title: ALMA Observations of a Quiescent Molecular Cloud in the Large Magellanic Cloud
question: How do size-linewidth, mass and virial properties of substructures differ between a quiescent LMC cloud (PCC) and the active 30 Dor cloud at matched 0.6 pc resolution?

data.bands: Band 6; 12CO(2-1), 13CO(2-1), C18O(2-1) plus continuum at 218 and 232 GHz
data.arrays: 12m, 7m (ACA) and total power; ACA not used in final analysis
data.angular_resolution: PCC native 1.81x1.24 arcsec; both clouds convolved to 2.5 arcsec (0.6 pc)
data.sensitivity: PCC 12CO rms 0.19 K (0.2 km/s channel) at 2.5 arcsec; continuum rms 0.21 mJy/beam

evidence.quote: we have also analyzed ALMA data for an additional cloud, 30Dor-10 (cite: Indebetouw:13)

what.value: Southern IR source 24um flux and far-IR luminosity 330 Lsun

evidence.quote: (cite: Seale:14) obtain a far-IR luminosity of 330$\pm$74 $L_\odot$ for this source

what.value: Virial-based LMC CO-to-H2 factor ~2.4 times Milky Way

evidence.quote: The CO(1–0) to H$_2$ conversion factor in the LMC is $\sim$2.4 times the factor for the Milky Way, based on the virial analysis of the MAGMA GMC catalog by (cite: Hughes:10).

recipe.method: Re-image 12m visibilities in CASA with clean, feather with TP, convolve to 2.5 arcsec
astrodendro on PPV cubes with bijection property measurement; derive R, L, M_vir, M_lum with bootstrap errors
key_parameters: local maxima >3 sigma, >=2.5 sigma above merge level, span at least two beams
assumptions: d=48 kpc; X2=4 (alpha_CO=4.3 x X2); M_vir=5 sigma_v^2 R/G

recipe.method: Power-law fits in log space with effective variance weighting using kmpfit, initial guess from linregress; exclude points below resolution
Derive Tex from 12CO peak, tau13, N(13CO), scale with H2/13CO=5e6; Monte Carlo errors
key_parameters: Tex floor 8 K, varied 6-10 K in Monte Carlo
assumptions: 12CO optically thick, common Tex, no beam dilution

recipe.method: Modified blackbody fit to 100-500 um SEDs with DUSTEM, beta in [0.8,2.8], Td in [5,55] K, 10% flux uncertainty

evidence.quote: we measure a CO(2–1) flux of 1691$\pm$10 Jy km s$^{-1}$
implying a CO(2–1)/$^{13}$CO(2–1) flux ratio of 13.5$\pm$1.6
The PCC and 30 Dor clouds have dust temperatures of $15.9\pm1.0$ K and $37\pm5$ K respectively
$\sigma_v$ for leaves ranges up to 0.95 km s$^{-1}$ for the PCC (3.20 km s$^{-1}$ for 30 Dor)

answer_key.quantity: Leaf share of kinetic energy PCC / 30 Dor

evidence.quote: the leaves as a whole contribute only 5.5% and 5.1% of the energy in PCC and 30 Dor respectively

answer_key.quantity: Total CO(1-0) gas mass of PCC (MAGMA)

evidence.quote: which translates to a molecular gas mass (including helium) of $2.7 \times 10^4$ $M_\odot$

not_stated_but_needed: astrodendro min_value/min_delta/min_npix numeric values in sigma units beyond description, and the rms used
Imaging weighting, robust, cell and image size, clean thresholds, line-free channels
TP-to-12m feather scaling and TP calibration details
Regridded 30 Dor cube specifics (velocity resolution handling, mosaic size)
Dust SED masks, background region definitions in detail
How data cubes were smoothed to 2.5 arcsec including primary beam correction
missing_for_reproduction: Table of structure properties not given
score_reason: Public data and named tools, but imaging and dendrogram parameters are incompletely specified.
rediscovery_reason: Public archival data, numeric results (scaling relations, line widths) and a mostly described recipe, though imaging parameters are missing.
